steps.instruction: Import the necessary TypeScript utilities and define the core Parser type interface.

steps.title: Create the basic parser function structure
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'parser' that takes a string parameter called 'input' and returns a ParserResult type. Use explicit type annotations for both the parameter and return type.
steps.hint: Remember to use the ParserResult type you defined earlier. The function should return a value of that type.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a properly typed parser function skeleton that can be built upon in later steps.

steps.title: Implement the string parser combinator
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'string' that takes a string literal as input and returns a Parser<string> that matches that exact string.
steps.hint: The function should return a parser function that checks if the input starts with the given literal. If it does, return success with the matched string; otherwise, return failure.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reusable 'string' function that creates parsers for specific string literals with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: The 'string' function is defined, takes a string parameter, returns a Parser<string>, and correctly implements the matching logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the string parser combinator. This is a fundamental building block for creating more complex parsers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns a Parser<string> and properly handles both successful matches and failures.
steps.feedbackWrong: The string parser combinator isn't implemented correctly. Check that your function takes a string parameter and returns a parser that matches that exact string.

steps.title: Add type-safe result handling
steps.instruction: Create a helper function named 'parse' that takes a Parser and input string, then returns a properly typed result using TypeScript's discriminated union pattern.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls the parser and returns either a success object with value or a failure object without value, using the 'success' property to discriminate.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'parse' function that provides type-safe handling of parser results with proper discriminated union return type.
successCriteria: The parse function is defined with proper TypeScript types, returns a discriminated union based on success status, and handles both success and failure cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your parse function correctly implements type-safe result handling with discriminated unions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your parse function returns a proper discriminated union type and handles both success and failure cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parse function should take a Parser and input string, then return a discriminated union result. Check the type definitions and implementation.

steps.title: Create the map parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a map function that transforms successful parser results while preserving type safety. Create a function named map that takes a parser and a transformation function, and returns a new parser with the transformed result type.
steps.hint: The map function should accept a parser of type T and a function that transforms T to U, then return a new parser of type U that applies the transformation on success.
steps.expectedOutcome: A map function that transforms parser results with proper TypeScript generics.
successCriteria: The map function is defined with type parameters T and U, accepts a Parser<T> and a function (T) => U, and returns a Parser<U>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the map combinator with proper type safety.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your map function uses generics and returns a parser that transforms the value on success.
steps.feedbackWrong: The map function is missing or incorrect. Review the expected type signature and transformation logic.

steps.title: Implement the choice parser combinator
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'choice' that takes an array of parsers and returns a new parser that tries each parser in sequence until one succeeds, with proper TypeScript union types for the result.
steps.hint: The function should accept an array of parsers with potentially different result types, and return a parser whose result type is a union of all possible parser result types.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'choice' function that combines multiple parsers with proper type union handling for the result type.
successCriteria: The 'choice' function is defined, accepts an array of parsers, returns a parser, and handles union types correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the choice combinator with proper type-safe alternatives.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function accepts an array of parsers and returns a parser with the correct union type.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. The choice combinator should try multiple parsers in sequence and return a parser with a union result type.

steps.title: Build the sequence parser combinator
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'sequence' that takes an array of parsers as input and returns a new parser that runs them in order, returning typed tuple results.
steps.hint: The sequence combinator should process each parser sequentially, accumulating results into a tuple while tracking the remaining input.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sequence function that accepts an array of parsers and returns a parser producing typed tuple results.
successCriteria: The sequence function is defined, accepts an array of parsers, and returns a parser that processes them in order with proper type handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the sequence combinator, enabling chaining of parsers with type-safe tuple results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your sequence function accepts an array of parsers and returns a new parser that processes them sequentially.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sequence combinator isn't quite right. Remember it should take parsers as input and return a parser that runs them in order, accumulating results.

steps.title: Create the many parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a function named 'many' that takes a parser and returns a new parser that applies it zero or more times, collecting results into a typed array.
steps.hint: The 'many' combinator should repeatedly apply the given parser until it fails, accumulating successful values in an array. Remember to handle the case where zero matches is valid (empty array).
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'many' function that returns a Parser<T[]> and correctly accumulates zero or more matches.
successCriteria: The 'many' function is implemented with proper TypeScript types and returns a parser that produces arrays of the inner parser's type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the 'many' combinator, which is essential for parsing repeated patterns.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your 'many' function correctly handles the zero-match case and accumulates results in an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match the requirements. Review how to create a parser combinator that applies another parser repeatedly.

steps.title: Add optional parser combinator
steps.instruction: Implement a combinator function named 'optional' that makes a parser optional, returning a result with proper optional type handling.
steps.hint: The optional combinator should accept a parser and return a new parser whose result type is T | undefined. If the inner parser succeeds, return its value; if it fails, return undefined without consuming input.
steps.expectedOutcome: The optional combinator function is defined with proper TypeScript type annotations, handling both success and failure cases while preserving the rest of the input.
successCriteria: The optional function is implemented, accepts a Parser<T>, returns a Parser<T | undefined>, and correctly handles parser success/failure without consuming input on failure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the optional parser combinator with proper TypeScript optional type handling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your optional combinator correctly returns undefined on failure without consuming input, and has the proper return type Parser<T | undefined>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The optional combinator implementation is missing or incorrect. Review the concept: it should wrap a parser to make it optional, returning the parsed value on success or undefined on failure without advancing the input.

successCriteria: A function named testParsers is created that includes calls to demonstrate the string, map, choice, sequence, many, and optional parser combinators.
